title: When and how a build sidecar restarts for new code
description: A sidecar restarts only when a byte of the files it actually loads (its import closure) differs from the closure it started with. Fleet machines receive edits of the build module continuously, so a burst of landings is coalesced into one restart: it waits until the closure was quiet for quietMilliseconds (a closure that is edited without a pause restarts after maximumDeferralMilliseconds at the latest), and two restarts are at least minimumIntervalMilliseconds apart, so ten landings in an hour cause one or two restarts, never ten, stops taking new work (drain), lets the work in flight finish for up to graceMilliseconds and then exits with status 75 so that its launcher starts it again with the new code. The `ready` role never defers its restart for a stage in flight (`serveDeferralMilliseconds` 0): its stage is a detached process that the next child adopts, so new code reaches a machine whose stage waits for hours at once, instead of after an hour. An edit that is reverted before the restart cancels it. The closure is looked at every watchMilliseconds. The restart is logged with the changed files and the time it was deferred. A role that holds a long computation whose results are keyed by the implementation that produced them (the graph server while it serves held requests) does not restart for a code change while that work is in flight: the restart waits until the work is done, for serveDeferralMilliseconds (8 h, used only for a role that reports no progress) at the latest counted from the first change, and a role that reports its progress (`work.progressAtMs`, the modification time of the progress file of its read) is never restarted while that progress advanced within progressStallMilliseconds: a long read is never cancelled by a clock, only by a stall, takes no new work while it waits and restarts at once when the work ends; the other roles keep the rule above.

Restart.description: H80 reload rule for every role: a role runs the code of its own closure at most `reloadWithinMilliseconds` (15 min) after the first edit of that closure. The first edit starts the clock, the quiet period coalesces the landings of a slot, the maximum deferral cuts a closure that is edited without a pause, and the drain (the agent stops taking work, the work in flight finishes for the grace, the actions it serves for other machines for at most `agent.drainMaximumMilliseconds` counted from the start of the drain) never lets the sum pass the bound. Only a role that reports the progress of a held computation (the graph server serving a read) is exempt while that progress advances, and it restarts when the progress stalls.

en.deferred: {role}: code of the sidecar edited ({files}); restarting after {quiet} s without a further change, after {maximum} s at the latest
en.draining: {role}: finishing the work in flight for up to {grace} s before the restart
en.waitingForServe: {role}: code changed ({files}); restarting when the serve in flight is done (at most {minutes} min)
en.reasonServeMaximum: maximum deferral of the serve reached
en.drainingServed: {role}: {running} remote action(s) served for other agents are still running after the grace; they are never aborted, waiting for them to end by their own deadline (at most {minutes} min) before the restart
en.drainBounded: {role}: {running} remote action(s) still run after {minutes} min, the bound of the drain; the restart goes on now

de.deferred: {role}: Code des Sidecars geändert ({files}); Neustart nach {quiet} s ohne weitere Änderung, spätestens nach {maximum} s
de.restarting: {role}: Code geändert, Neustart (verzögert um {deferred} s, {reason}; geändert: {files})
de.draining: {role}: beende die laufende Arbeit (bis zu {grace} s) vor dem Neustart
de.waitingForServe: {role}: Code geändert ({files}); Neustart, sobald der laufende Serve fertig ist (höchstens {minutes} min)
de.drainingServed: {role}: {running} für andere Agenten bediente Remote-Aktion(en) laufen nach der Frist noch; sie werden nie abgebrochen, Neustart erst nach ihrem Ende durch ihre eigene Frist (höchstens {minutes} min)
de.drainBounded: {role}: {running} Remote-Aktion(en) laufen nach {minutes} min, der Grenze des Auslaufens, noch; der Neustart geht jetzt weiter
